subject: Commitment remediation catalog and escalation summary - BlueSky Retail
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@blueskyretail.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Timothy Shaw <t.shaw@blueskyretail.com>, procurement@blueskyretail.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Timeline concern — July evaluation window slipping

Jonas —

Quick note from our side: the internal security review and the vendor security questionnaire pushed the evaluation start by two weeks. That cascades into our pilots and procurement sign-off window.

We still intend to run the PoC, but we need a revised MAP and a clear list of dealkeeper dates so procurement can lock in budget this quarter. Can you provide: 1) an updated MAP with new milestones; 2) the evaluation plan adjusted for a late July start; and 3) a risk catalog that says what happens if we lose a week here or there?

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Digital Ops
BlueSky Retail

Attachments: none

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena@blueskyretail.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline concern — July evaluation window slipping

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up. I built a quick remediation catalog that maps the original MAP milestones to contingency actions and owner assignments. High-level:

- Move evaluation kickoff to 26 Jul (was 12 Jul), compress internal checkpoints and extend parallel validation to reduce overall runway by 1 week.
- Apply an acceptance gate for data ingest so procurement can sign while we run isolated evals on synthetic data.
- Add a one-week credit for pilot extension in case the security re-run adds time (we'll confirm approvals).

I attached a draft (BSR_MAP_v2.xlsx) and a CSV risk log that lists probable slippage causes and immediate mitigations. Laura and Rishi are looped for technical and commercial impacts.

Please review and flag anything missing. If that looks ok, we'll re-baseline and I will escalate to our VP for formal approval of the one-week credit.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BSR_MAP_v2.xlsx, timeline_risk_log.csv

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Elena Torres <elena@blueskyretail.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline concern — July evaluation window slipping

Elena, Jonas —

Quick technical note: compressing the checkpoints is feasible but increases load on our validation team during tokenization and eval runs. Recommendation: keep the data ingest acceptance separate (so procurement can sign) and run two parallel eval tracks: 1) integration track (lower fidelity, higher speed) to show end-to-end flow; 2) quality track (full fidelity) that runs longer but starts with a small subset.

I've updated the evaluation_plan_v3.pdf to reflect the two-track approach and added mandatory sign-offs per track. This should reduce the perceived risk to procurement while preserving our ability to validate quality.

Laura
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: evaluation_plan_v3.pdf

From: Timothy Shaw <t.shaw@blueskyretail.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, Elena Torres <elena@blueskyretail.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline concern — July evaluation window slipping

Thanks — that approach seems acceptable but procurement needs the formal MAP and a timeline with clear purchase triggers. Two asks: 1) confirm the final re-baselined close date target (we need a date to put in the purchase requisition), and 2) confirm whether Redwood can commit to a 7-day pilot extension credit if security re-test causes delay.

If you can get those answers to procurement by next Tuesday we can keep the internal approvals on track.

-Timothy
Sr. Manager, Procurement
BlueSky Retail

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@blueskyretail.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: request for pilot extension credit and formal re-baseline approval (BSR-4821)

Marissa —

Heads up on BSR-4821 (BlueSky). Evaluation window slipped ~2 weeks due to security questionnaire re-run. Customer is willing to proceed if we: 1) re-baseline the MAP to a 26 Jul kickoff; 2) provide a formal one-week pilot extension credit to cover potential security re-tests; and 3) confirm final close target of 30 Sep 2027 for procurement paperwork.

I've attached the updated MAP, the evaluation plan, and the consolidated risk catalog. Asking for your approval to: (A) authorize a single 7-day pilot credit (no price changes), and (B) sign off on the re-baselined close target so I can provide procurement a date.

If approved, I'll update the contract route and inform procurement. If you want different terms (e.g., an SLA exception or additional credits) say so and I'll escalate to finance.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: BSR_MAP_v2.xlsx, evaluation_plan_v3.pdf, timeline_risk_log.csv

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@blueskyretail.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Approval granted — one-week pilot credit and re-baseline (BSR-4821)

Jonas —

Approved. I authorize: 1) a one-week pilot extension credit; and 2) the re-baselined close target of 2027-09-30 for procurement and internal forecasting. Conditions: we mark the MAP with the new checkpoints and require weekly sync notes from the Solutions Architect while the quality track completes. Laura — please add a short progress checklist to the MAP that Jonas can paste into the procurement submission.

Jonas, confirm once you update contract language and route the procurement deliverables; I'll notify finance to accept the credit (no accounting write-off required given pilot status).

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
